subject: ACME competitive bake-off: test plan, success criteria, and timeline
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.co@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (ACME bake-off)

Thanks again for taking the call today, Olivia — appreciate the clear context on ACME's search assistant pilot. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

Summary of needs:
- Real-time semantic search (sub-200ms for 512-token queries) against a 1M-document corpus
- Relevance precision target: P@5 >= 0.88 on ACME test queries
- Cost target: baseline inference cost < $0.0009/token for serving POCs
- Data residency: US-only; no model training on customer data

Competitive context you shared:
- You're running exploratory tests with hyperscaler-managed endpoints (Company X) and a smaller inference provider (Vendor Y). Top concerns are latency at scale and predictable per-query cost.

Proposed bake-off scope (high level):
1) Latency & throughput: 95th/99th latency at target QPS (50 qps sustained, 200 burst)
2) Relevance: run your 500 canonical queries and measure P@1/P@5/NDCG vs your current baseline
3) Cost: measured cost per 1k queries and cost-per-token for generation steps
4) Failure modes & fallbacks: cold-start, KV cache warmup, degraded model variant behavior

Owners & timeline (proposal):
- Redwood lead: Aditya Rao (runtime & infra) — responsible for environment setup and metrics collection
- Redwood sales/CS: Marissa Cole — PM for coordination and acceptance criteria
- ACME technical lead: Olivia Chen — provide canonical query set and sample corpus
- Procurement/legal: Neha Kapoor (Redwood) — SOW + quick T&Cs

Proposed timeline:
- Deliverables: test harness + instructions by Wed 2026-08-05
- Run bake-off: 2026-08-10 -> 2026-08-12 (3 days of tests, measurements nightly)
- Wrap / results review: 2026-08-14

Next actions for ACME:
- Share canonical queries (CSV) and a 10k-document sample of your corpus (scrubbed) by Friday 2026-08-01
- Confirm legal procurement contact for SOW

Attachments: I attached a draft requirements spreadsheet and Redwood performance profile for reference.

If that looks good, we'll lock the timeline and I'll kick off Aditya to provision the test environment.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.co@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0134

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.co@redwood.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (ACME bake-off)

Great notes, Marissa — I'll take point on the runtime/test harness. A couple of technical clarifications and what I plan to ship for the bake-off:

1) Environment topology:
- We'll run two arms: Redwood-hosted inference (our managed nodes in us-west-2) and a Redwood private deployment configured to mimic your on-prem constraints if you want to test data residency. For comparison vs hyperscaler endpoints, please confirm the endpoint types and auth tokens if you want us to pull telemetry from their APIs.

2) Test harness & metrics:
- Tools: wrk-style load driver for QPS, and a small Python harness for relevance scoring and cost aggregation.
- Metrics: 50/200 QPS profiles, p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens generated, cost-per-1k-queries, and memory/GPU utilization during runs.
\3) Model variants to evaluate:
- Redwood-curated open LLM (quantized int8) tuned for retrieval-augmented generation
- Smaller low-latency variant (quantized int4) for strict latency targets
- A fallback model for degraded capacity tests (cheaper but lower context length)
\4) Success criteria (suggested):
- Latency: p95 < 200ms on 512-token queries at 50 qps
- Relevance: P@5 >= 0.88 vs ACME canonical set
- Cost: cost-per-query <= your in-house target (we'll compute after we see sample data)
\5) Data & security:
- We'll only ingest scrubbed samples you provide. If ACME needs an NDA or encryption-at-rest keys, ping Neha and Legal.

Plan to deliver a test harness repo + runbook by Wed 2026-08-05. I'll include Jupyter notebooks with scoring logic so your team can reproduce locally.

-Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acme.com>

Cc: Jorge Alvarez <jorge.alvarez@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (ACME bake-off)

Thanks, Marissa and Aditya — this looks like the right approach. Quick notes from ACME: 

- We'll share the 500 canonical queries as discussed; those are ready. Expect the CSV by EOD Friday 2026-08-01.
- We can provide a 10k sample corpus (redacted) but need to confirm the scrubbed process. Please include the scrub steps in the runbook.
- For competitive baseline, we are testing Company X (managed endpoint) and Vendor Y. I can share APIToken for Vendor Y test account; for Company X we'll provide a summary report (they don't allow shared tokens).
- On metrics: make sure the scoring notebook logs per-query answers and highlights samples where our baseline outperforms Redwood — we'll need that for product-level comparisons.

Legal/procurement: I'll loop in our procurement lead if we finalize the SOW. For now, please send the SOW draft and estimated committed hours so my team can review.

Looking forward to the runbook.

Olivia

All — thanks for the quick turn. Summarizing agreed next steps and owners so we have a single source of truth:

ACTIONS (owners):
- ACME: deliver canonical queries CSV + 10k scrubbed sample corpus by EOD 2026-08-01 (Olivia) — RECEIVED
- Redwood: deliver test harness repo + runbook + scoring notebook by 2026-08-05 (Aditya)
- Redwood Legal/SOW: finalize SOW + send DocuSign link by 2026-08-03 (Neha)

Success criteria (finalized):

- P@5 >= 0.88 on ACME canonical set
